tooltips.cagr: Compound annual growth rate: the constant yearly return that would turn your total deposits into the current value over the holding period.
tooltips.openingBalance: Money already in the fund before the provider's deposit history begins: the first recorded balance minus the deposits listed up to it. It counts as invested, not as profit, alongside total deposits in profit, ROI and CAGR.

fire.title: Early-Retirement Calculator

hint.expenses: One row per recurring expense. Use "one-time" for a wedding, a car, or a big trip. Loans belong in the Loans section.

hint.portfolios: Order matters: it sets both the order accounts are filled and the order they are drawn down. A goal of 0 means the account never receives deposits.

help.base_problem: Which question to answer. Retire ASAP: the earliest month that works. Check-up: does the plan hold if you retire at a given age? The last two find how much better cash flow, or how much extra return, you would need to retire at a given age. Zeke's own site currently fails on those two, so this app solves them as their descriptions say.
help.wanted_retire_age: The age you want to retire at. A check-up retires you exactly here; the last two modes search for what it takes to get here.
help.base_problem_max_age: The latest retirement age the search will consider. If no month before this age works, the plan reports that it could not reach its goals.
help.base_problem_cash_improve: The largest monthly improvement (more income or less spending, in today's shekels) the search may assume.
help.base_problem_risk_increase: The largest number of percentage points the search may add to your portfolios' expected annual return.
help.pensionName: Only labels the charts and the pension rows.
help.gender: Sets the statutory retirement age, when Bituach Leumi's old-age pension starts, and the annuity factor that turns a pension balance into a monthly pension.
help.dateOfBirth: Every age in the plan comes from this: retirement, age 60, the statutory age and the end of the projection at 81. Only the month matters.
help.is_american: Zeke's form asks for it, but in every test it changed nothing, so the model ignores it.
help.pensionTake: Adds a partner: their age, their pension fund and their Bituach Leumi pension join the plan.
help.retireRule: How sure (80–100%) you want to be that the portfolios do not run out before the pension starts. From the Trinity study at 75% stocks. A higher value means a lower return is assumed for withdrawal portfolios after you retire, so you retire later.
help.prati_hishtalmut_order: After retirement, which pot pays the bills first: the taxed portfolios (25% tax on the profit you withdraw) or the Keren Hishtalmut (tax-free). Only the order changes.
help.cashBuffer: How much to keep in the checking account. Each month's surplus tops it up to this first. After retirement it is the last money spent. It earns no return.
help.balance: What is in the checking account today. It earns no return.
help.creditLimit: How far the account may go below zero. A month that would need more is counted as not covered.

flow.start: Now: from this month. From early retirement: from the month after you stop working. From a date: from that month on. One-time: a single payment in one month.
flow.startDate: The month the row starts, or for a one-time row, the month it is paid. Only the month matters. A one-time date in the past is ignored.
flow.end: Forever: to the end of the projection (age 81). Until early retirement: through your last working month. Until a date: through that month. Until age 60: through the month the main retiree turns 60.
flow.endDate: The last month the row is paid (included).
flow.rise: How much the amount grows each year beyond inflation, in %. 0 keeps it fixed in today's money. Growth counts from the row's first month.
flow.description: A name for the row, shown in the charts.

help.expenseSum: The amount in today's shekels: per month, or the whole payment for a one-time row. Loan repayments go in the Loans section, not here.
help.incomeSum: Take-home pay or other income after tax, in today's shekels: per month, or the whole sum for a one-time row. Your pension and Bituach Leumi are added by the plan; don't enter them here.
help.portfolioDesignation: Funds living expenses: drawn on to pay the bills after retirement. Earmarked for a goal: grows untouched and is never used for living. Recognised annuity (Gemel le'hashkaa only): turned in full at age 60 into a tax-free pension for the retiree or the partner; before 60 it acts like a goal account.
help.portfolio_type: Return, fees and tax are the same for every type. Only Gemel le'hashkaa differs: deposits are capped at ₪76,449 a year, and only it can become a recognised annuity.
help.portfolioBalance: What the portfolio is worth today.
help.portfolio_deposit: The most that goes into this portfolio each month; blank means no limit. Each month's surplus fills the portfolios in list order.
help.portfolio_goal: Deposits stop once the balance reaches this. 0 means this portfolio never receives deposits, and the surplus stays in checking, earning nothing.
help.portfolioInterest: Expected annual return beyond inflation, before fees. A withdrawal portfolio switches to a lower return, set by the confidence level, once you retire.
help.portfolioFee: Annual management fee, in %. It is taken off the return each year.
help.portfolioProfitFraction: What share of today's balance is unrealised profit. Withdrawals pay 25% tax on their profit share, so a higher share means more must be withdrawn for each shekel spent.
help.portfolio_fifo_lifo: Which purchases a withdrawal is treated as selling. Proportional: every shekel carries the same share of profit. FIFO: oldest first (most profit, more tax early on). LIFO: newest first (least profit, less tax early on).
help.portfolioDescription: A name for the portfolio, shown in the charts.
help.pensionBalance: What the pension fund holds today, as on your latest statement.
help.pensionDeposit: The full monthly deposit: your part, the employer's and severance.
help.pensionFee1: Annual management fee on the balance, in %.
help.pensionFee2: Management fee on each deposit, in %.
help.pensionInterest: Expected annual return of the pension fund beyond inflation, before fees.
help.pension_tactics: When the balance becomes a monthly pension. All at 60: an earlier start, so a smaller pension. All at the statutory age: a larger pension, later. Split: the recognised (tax-free) part from 60, the entitling (taxed) part from the statutory age.
help.percentage_mukeret: The share of the monthly pension that is a recognised annuity (קצבה מוכרת), which is free of income tax. The rest (מזכה) is taxed as income, with an exemption from the statutory age.
help.pensionEndType: When deposits into the fund stop. Usually when you stop working (at early retirement).
help.pensionEndDate: The last month a deposit is made (included).
help.withdraw_pizuim: Take your current employer's severance as cash when you retire instead of leaving it in the pension. Part of it is tax-free, depending on how many years you worked there; the rest is taxed.
help.work_start_year: The year you started at your current employer. It sets your years of service, and so how much of the severance is tax-free.
help.kerenBalance: What the fund holds today. Withdrawals from a Keren Hishtalmut are tax-free in this model.
help.kerenDeposit: Monthly deposit, including the employer's part. Use 0 for a fund you no longer pay into.
help.kerenInterest: Expected annual return beyond inflation, before fees.
help.kerenType: Managed track: Zeke's calculator adds 0.6% a year to the fee you enter. It is his own assumption and he doesn't explain it. IRA: only the fee you enter is charged. If the fee you enter is already your fund's full fee (as on your statement), choose IRA.
help.kerenEndType: When deposits stop. Usually at early retirement.
help.kerenEndDate: The last month a deposit is made (included).
help.debtStartDate: When the loan was taken. A loan taken in the past is repaid on its original schedule from that date. A loan whose term already ended is ignored.
help.debtInterest: The loan's annual interest rate, in %.
help.debtInitialSum: The amount originally borrowed, not what is left today.
help.debtTotalPeriod: The loan's original length, in years.
help.debtType: Spitzer: equal monthly payments. Balloon: no payments; interest builds up and everything is repaid at the end. Grace: interest only each month, with the principal repaid at the end. What is still owed is taken off your net worth.
help.realestateValue: What the property is worth today, your home included. It counts in your net worth, but it pays no rent and is never sold; enter rent as an income row.
help.realestateRise: Expected annual rise in value beyond inflation, in %.
